senses.definition: (dated, dialectal) A thicket; a small wood or grove.

quotes.text: All this herd sire Lamorak / and on the morne sir lamorak took his hors and rode vnto the forest / and there he mette with two knyghtes houynge vnder the wood shawe
quotes.reference: 1485, Sir Thomas Malory, chapter XII, in Le Morte Darthur, book IX:

quotes.text: Thenne said sire kay I requyre you lete vs preue this aduenture / I shal not fayle you said sir Gaherys / and soo they rode that tyme tyl a lake / that was that tyme called the peryllous lake / And there they abode vnder the shawe of the wood
quotes.reference: 1485, Sir Thomas Malory, chapter XXXIX, in Le Morte Darthur, book IX:

quotes.text: The snows are fled away, leaves on the shaws, / And grasses in the mead renew their birth,
quotes.reference: 1936, Alfred Edward Housman, More Poems, V, lines 1-2:

senses.definition: (Scotland) The leaves and tops of vegetables, especially potatoes and turnips.

quotes.text: Up here the hills were brave with the beauty and the heat of it, but the hayfield was still all a crackling dryness and in the potato park beyond the biggings the shaws drooped red and rusty already.
